subject: ss-cardiology
title: Cardiac Tumours and Heart in Systemic Disease

steps.tx: **Cardiac myxoma** is the most common primary cardiac tumor in adults accounting for **50%** of cases, typically arising from the **fossa ovalis** border in the left atrium in **75%**, presenting with intracardiac obstruction, embolic phenomena, and constitutional symptoms. A mobile pedunculated mass prolapsing through the mitral valve produces an early diastolic tumor plop.

rows: Pedunculated tumor prolapses into mitral orifice
Positional dyspnea, syncope, tumor plop sound
Friable gelatinous fragments or surface thrombi detach
Ischemic stroke, retinal infarction, splenic infarcts
Fever, weight loss, arthralgia, elevated ESR and CRP

steps.tx: Echo frame shows a bright rounded mass on a stalk fixed at the septum swinging toward the mitral opening during filling. The lesion sits in the left atrium and briefly plugs the valve, matching **myxoma** behavior from the lesson. Recognizing this mobile **mass** explains positional breathlessness plus embolic risk and favors prompt surgical **removal**.
steps.say: The echo shows a mobile left atrial mass attached by a stalk to the septum and prolapsing toward the mitral valve. That motion can obstruct filling and produce an early diastolic sound while fragments may embolize. Constitutional signs can accompany the triad in the lesson. Seeing stalk attachment and valve approach on the image points to myxoma and the need for surgical excision.

vis.alt: Apical echo shows a stalked left atrial mass prolapsing toward the mitral valve.
vis.caption: Echo shows stalked atrial mass approaching the mitral valve. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Carney complex** is an autosomal dominant syndrome caused by **PRKAR1A** mutations on chromosome **1**, combining recurrent cardiac myxomas, spotty skin pigmentation (lentigines), and endocrine hyperactivity including primary pigmented nodular adrenocortical disease. Myxomas in Carney complex are frequently multicentric, atypical in location, and carry high recurrence rates.

left.title: Sporadic Cardiac Myxoma
points: Absence of genetic mutations or syndrome features

right.title: Carney Complex Myxoma
points: PRKAR1A mutation, spotty skin pigmentation, PPNAD

steps.tx: **Papillary fibroelastoma** is the most common primary tumor of **cardiac valves**, resembling a sea anemone on echocardiography with multiple papillary fronds and posing high embolic stroke risk requiring surgical excision. These avascular tumors typically arise on the downstream side of aortic and mitral valve leaflets.
steps.say: Papillary fibroelastoma is the most common primary tumor of cardiac valves, resembling a sea anemone on echocardiography with multiple papillary fronds and posing high embolic stroke risk requiring surgical excision. These avascular tumors typically arise on the downstream side of aortic and mitral valve leaflets.

rows: Downstream or either side of valve leaflet
Sea anemone fronds with shimmering border
Shaggy, mobile, amorphous mass with tissue destruction
Normal leaflet mobility; rarely causes regurgitation

steps.tx: **Cardiac rhabdomyoma** is the most frequent primary cardiac tumor in infants and children, strongly associated with **tuberous sclerosis** driven by mutations in TSC**1** or TSC**2**, characterized by spontaneous regression. These benign hamartomas arise within ventricular myocardium, managed conservatively unless severe outflow obstruction occurs.

These benign hamartomas arise within ventricular myocardium, managed conservatively unless severe outflow obstruction occurs.

nodes.label: Tuberous Sclerosis Complex: Mutations in TSC1 (Hamartin) or TSC2
Spontaneous Tumor Regression Across Early Childhood (or mTOR Inhibitor)

steps.tx: **Cardiac angiosarcoma** is the most common primary **malignant cardiac tumor** in adults, typically located in the right atrium and pericardium with early hemorrhagic pericardial effusion, tamponade, and widespread metastases. Angiosarcomas exhibit aggressive local invasion of the vena cava, tricuspid valve, and coronary arteries.
steps.say: Cardiac angiosarcoma is the most common primary malignant cardiac tumor in adults, typically located in the right atrium and pericardium with early hemorrhagic pericardial effusion, tamponade, and widespread metastases. Angiosarcomas demonstrate rapid aggressive local invasion of the vena cava, tricuspid valve, and coronary arteries, and they invade surrounding tissues rapidly.

nodes.label: Malignant Endothelial Neoplasm Arising in Right Atrium

steps.tx: The scan shows a bulky **right atrial mass** invading downward into the vena cava with a large **pericardial effusion** around the heart. Nodular **lung metastases** dot the nearby lung. This invasive right sided mass with fluid plus distant spread matches the lesson pattern for **malignant** disease such as angiosarcoma rather than a benign stalked tumour, so invasion plus effusion plus spread drives urgency.
steps.say: Look at the right side of the heart. A rough mass fills the atrium and extends into the great vein below. Fluid rings the heart. Small nodules sit out in the lung. One finding alone is concerning, but mass plus vessel invasion plus fluid plus distant nodules together point to aggressive malignant disease. That is why the lesson stresses location, invasion and spread when judging a cardiac mass.

vis.alt: Axial heart scan shows right atrial mass with vein invasion, surrounding fluid and lung nodules.
vis.caption: Invasive right sided mass with fluid and spread Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Metastatic tumors** to the heart are **20** to **40** times more frequent than primary cardiac tumors, most often originating from lung cancer, breast cancer, **melanoma** which has the highest propensity for myocardial metastasis, and lymphoma. Direct venous extension occurs via the inferior vena cava in renal cell carcinoma.

rows: Direct contiguous invasion or retrograde lymphatic
Direct intraluminal cavoatrial tumor thrombus up IVC

steps.tx: **Carcinoid heart disease** occurs in patients with neuroendocrine tumors and hepatic metastases due to circulating vasoactive **serotonin** **5**-HT, causing plaque-like fibrous thickening of tricuspid and pulmonic valves leading to severe tricuspid regurgitation. Left-sided valves are spared because serotonin is metabolized by pulmonary monoamine oxidases.

Left-sided valves are spared because serotonin is metabolized by pulmonary monoamine oxidases.

nodes.label: Hepatic Metastases Bypass First-Pass Portal Clearance
Vasoactive Serotonin (5-HT) Released into Systemic Venous Circulation
Endocardial Fibroblast Proliferation & Plaque Deposition on TV/PV
Severe Tricuspid Regurgitation; Left Valves Spared by Pulmonary MAO

steps.tx: Rheumatoid arthritis and **systemic lupus erythematosus** involve the heart through pericarditis, myocarditis, and **Libman-Sacks endocarditis** characterized by verrucous, nonbacterial valvular lesions on both surfaces of mitral and aortic leaflets. Libman-Sacks vegetations are strongly associated with antiphospholipid antibodies and carry embolic risk. Comprehensive clinical evaluation requires careful correlation with serial electrocardiographic tracings and hemodynamic parameters.

left.title: Libman-Sacks Endocarditis (SLE/APS)
points: Located on both surfaces of leaflets and commissures
Predisposes to arterial thromboembolism and secondary IE

right.title: Rheumatic Endocarditis
points: Small verrucae along lines of leaflet closure
Accompanied by commissural fusion and chordal shortening
Leads to progressive mitral stenosis over decades
Triggered by Group A Streptococcus molecular mimicry
